status.title: Monty on the Run
status.build: monty_on_the_run_sprites.nex (as published in nxc 1.0: enemies in their own ink and Monty in white as sprites over the two XOR plotters, the attribute painter off; four cheats)
status.software: replay IDENTICAL on 61,198 frames (57,105 figure checks, 13.7M pixels); unit cases incl. four CPU speeds; 10 negatives detected
status.hardware: KS3 (System/Next 26.11a): played by the owner 2026-11-27, the text line under the play area is garbled (to be fixed); Tang board: loads with automap on, reaches the menu (play through the Sinclair keys 6-0)

techniques.target: survey readers: only the plotters' own read-modify-write; no collision reads of screen pixels
the enemy (0xB4F5) and Monty (0xEFE4) XOR plotters kept; two sprites per figure over the drawn image, the painter's attribute writes NOPed
Sinclair 48K ROM as alt ROM image 1, hooks at 0x386E
28 MHz inside each hook, the caller's NR 7 kept on the stack and put back

results.scope: 1 rzxarchive recording (61,198 frames, 157 rooms); unit cases for the enemy, Monty, room, new game and menu hooks at four CPU speeds; 10 negatives; no hardware timing

pacing.coverage: Hook T over the first 3,000 frames of the recording in the simulator; no JNext or hardware timing.
pacing.result: About 1.9% of the frame budget: enemy hook ~37.8k T, Monty ~12.6k T at 28 MHz, run about one frame in 4.75.

dependencies.coverage: Every screen reader in the first 15,000 frames (survey) and the whole recording's plotter, painter, room and lift-block writes.
dependencies.result: No routine reads screen pixels for collisions: the XORs stay on the ULA; the attribute painter's writes are the clash and are removed.

feasibility.decision: Enemies in their own ink and Monty in white as sprites over the kept XOR plotters, the attribute painter off (the standing default).
feasibility.next_experiment: A human recording reaching the later caverns and the escape: replay IDENTICAL with every negative control caught.
